note: How a scene with a purpose plays (owner, Oct 15, evening: a setup, a person with a purpose, stakes, and an exchange that plays to resolved or refused). Moves only: no sentence is here; the English engine words each move from data/english/parts/scene-talk.json. A purpose names what the asker states and the player's four reply moves; `follow` is how the asker answers each reply move, chosen by the asker's traits (each candidate's pulls, summed over the asker's trait levels; the highest wins, so no roll decides it); `again` is the player's four replies to that answer; `close` ends the exchange by its outcome. A yes or a no never ends a talk: the asker answers it, and the exchange closes only when the purpose is resolved or refused. A purpose may carry its own `follow` and `again`; the engine reads them before the shared ones, so a family talk never borrows a vote's answers.

rounds.checkedAgainst: Player replies before the exchange must close; the owner asked for multi-exchange scenes (Oct 15, night), and five rounds let a bargain, a push-back and a lie play out on the bench.

baseWeight.checkedAgainst: A follow-up move's weight before trait pulls, so a move with no pulling traits can still be chosen.

outcomes.note: What each reply move does to the purpose: resolved closes it, refused closes it the other way, open keeps the exchange going.

again.note: The player's four replies to the asker's answer, by that answer's move.

close.note: How the asker ends the exchange, by outcome: never a bare goodbye after a question was answered.

lie.note: A lie is caught only when the asker holds the record that contradicts it (fact knows-truth, naming its source); otherwise it is believed and stands until the record surfaces. No roll decides it.

keys.note: The fallback for any situation with no purpose yet (owner, Oct 16: the English engine builds every conversation, crudely until it is written). One arc per situation key; pieces whose use names purpose "*" and the key serve it, and an authored purpose always wins.
